doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

chapter: Meeting Joe and life with the Basie band
title: Jim Crow on the road: she noticed nothing
summary: Fillius asks about segregation on tour; Jillean says she never noticed any and had misunderstood the question at first.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In the interview we had this morning with Joe and Clark Terry, they talked about Jim Crowism in their travels. Did you run into that at all with the Basie band?
I didn’t. If we did I didn’t notice it.
You didn’t notice it? Well you probably didn’t then.
I didn’t notice it. I didn’t think about it. And I would not go to a place where obviously it would not be approved that Joe and I were together.
Well I wasn’t referring to that.

Oh, no, no, no, no, no. That Jim Crow is directed against the blacks. Where, well for example, the bands that used to travel in the south had terrible trouble eating and finding places to stay. And I’m reminded of Calloway who eventually bought himself a rail car, which served as their home every place they went. And I just wondered if the Basie band ran into that, because I’ve never heard of any problem with the Basie band.
I really didn’t notice anything like that. It went over my head if it was there.
